claims.text: A machine-learning-based high-throughput exploration approach can identify RHEA compositions with increased intrinsic strength.
A machine-learning-based high-throughput exploration approach can identify RHEA compositions with improved ductility.
A machine-learning-based high-throughput exploration approach can identify RHEA compositions with reduced density.
Multi-principal refractory alloys can incorporate elements such as Nb, Mo, Ta, V, and W.
An adaptive machine-learning workflow can systematically propose and screen candidate RHEA compositions.
Computational or small-scale experimental feedback on mechanical properties can be used to refine the candidate-selection workflow.
Using controlled synthesis and heat-treatment protocols will ensure consistent microstructures across candidate formulations.
The proposed workflow will favor stable, predominantly BCC or B2 phases with controlled microstructures and precipitate distributions.
The proposed phase and microstructural state will enhance solid-solution strengthening.
The proposed phase and microstructural state will promote ductility while reducing density.
Machine-learning models can exploit correlations between composition and yield strength or ductility to guide targeted compositional exploration.
Selection of favorable phases and elemental substitutions can increase strength and reduce weight without compromising toughness.
The method is predicted to produce RHEAs with yield strength 5–15% higher than baseline compositions.
The method is predicted to reduce RHEA density by up to several percent relative to baseline compositions.
The method is predicted to retain or enhance ductility relative to baseline compositions.
The approach depends on having sufficient, high-quality training data.
The approach may not transfer directly to compositions outside the explored domain.
Predicted mechanical and density benefits depend on data quantity, data quality, and alloy-processing conditions.
Extrapolation into compositional spaces far from the training data can produce prediction errors.
